sections.label: Forward Singapore themes and shared responsibilities
sections.summary: Feedback from Singaporeans is being used to work on three themes and shared responsibilities for a refreshed compact.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have received, from Singaporeans, many useful insights for policy formulations, suggestions of solutions and offers for action, all of which will help us build a better and stronger Singapore together.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have been working on three broad themes: how to create more opportunities for Singapore and Singaporeans; how to provide better assurances for Singaporeans in a more uncertain future; and how to strengthen our sense of solidarity as one people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Besides these three themes, we are also deliberating over the shared responsibilities that individual Singaporeans, families, communities and companies, should uphold as part of the refreshed compact, so that we can better tackle the challenges ahead and seize new opportunities for Singapore and for our people.

sections.label: Public registration for Forward Singapore sessions
sections.summary: The public and organisations can register interest in the sessions through the Forward Singapore website, with the exercise planned to finish by the middle of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I welcome members of the public and organisations to register their interest to participate in these sessions through the Forward Singapore website.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We plan to complete the exercise by the middle of next year.

sections.label: Publishing and milestones for Forward Singapore feedback
sections.summary: Section 377A will not be a key part of Forward Singapore, and suitable platforms and possible mid-term milestones like the Budget will be used to publish and respond to feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And it was a result of these engagements and conversations that led to the Government's announcement of what it hopes to do at the National Day Rally this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we do not intend for section 377A and the issues around it to be a key part of our Forward Singapore platform, because these started after the conversations had already begun.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, on the process and what we will do to put down and publish the conversations that we had with Singaporeans – whether it is a White Paper or whether there are other platforms – we will review and study what are the suitable platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will not rule out having some mid-term milestones where we might very well decide to compile, consolidate some of the feedback and respond to them earlier, even before the end of the exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, we have the Budget next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, when we engage Singaporeans through Forward Singapore over the course of the next few months, we might very well use the Budget next year as an interim milestone where we can compile the views and feedback from people and then respond to them with some announcements without having to wait all the way till the end of the exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But, certainly, by the completion of the exercise, we will find suitable platforms in which we can pool together all the feedback, suggestions and ideas we have collated and make sure that these are adequately surfaced through appropriate means.
